description: Fail-closed route kind, rendered-view, navigation/direct-entry and unreferenced page classifications for Issue #360.

route_kind_overrides.rationale: The authenticated Wiki media index returns the JSON media-picker payload used by the editorial screen and is not a standalone rendered page.
The robots.txt route returns a machine-readable crawler policy resource and is not a user-facing rendered screen or navigation destination.
The sitemap.xml route renders an XML discovery resource for crawlers; it is intentionally machine-discovered rather than linked as a portal screen.

direct_entry_routes.rationale: This token-bound confirmation screen is entered from the one-time email-change confirmation link, not from persistent portal navigation.
This token-bound recovery screen is entered from the one-time email-change recovery link, not from persistent portal navigation.
Authentication middleware routes an identity with a pending MFA session to this challenge screen; it is intentionally absent from normal navigation.
This unauthenticated account-recovery entry accepts the identity recovery key and is intentionally reached as a recovery workflow rather than account navigation.
Managed public pages are selected by database-backed slug and linked from configured content/navigation data, so no single literal route reference can enumerate this dynamic screen.
This token-bound password-reset screen is entered from the one-time recovery email link and is intentionally absent from persistent portal navigation.

direct_entry_route_patterns.rationale: Locale-less compatibility aliases intentionally remain direct-entry routes for existing external deep links; internal navigation uses the matching canonical localized route.

unreferenced_page_classifications.rationale: Laravel resolves the status-specific 403 error template by the resources/views/errors/{status}.blade.php exception-rendering convention, so no literal view() reference is expected.
Laravel resolves the status-specific 404 error template by the resources/views/errors/{status}.blade.php exception-rendering convention, so no literal view() reference is expected.
Laravel resolves the status-specific 429 error template by the resources/views/errors/{status}.blade.php exception-rendering convention, so no literal view() reference is expected.
Laravel resolves the status-specific 500 error template by the resources/views/errors/{status}.blade.php exception-rendering convention, so no literal view() reference is expected.
Laravel resolves the status-specific 503 error template by the resources/views/errors/{status}.blade.php exception-rendering convention, so no literal view() reference is expected.

This noindex design prototype has no delivered route, controller or parent-view reference and remains intentionally unreachable until the allowlisted authenticated homepage-template preview is implemented or the prototype is retired.
evidence: Issue #244 audited administrator homepage template selector
